summary: Adapt the existing RuntimeConfig, binder and backend Plan boundary for consumed configuration, scoped resource ceilings and measured backend selection; extend existing dense tiled Metal lowering for BF16/F16 storage.
rule: No parallel IR/runtime, silent numeric relaxation, ignored constraint, or pretend absent-backend execution. llama.cpp is the performance oracle; existing Proxima is the before-change baseline. Every reported latency retains raw samples and CoV%.

summary: Luna owns bounded config and tiled edits; Sol owns public cross-backend planning, binding and allocation semantics. Root integrates and reads actual diffs/payloads.
reason: The execution seam changes a public contract across tensor and driver crates with allocation and numerical correctness obligations; this capability envelope selects Sol before execution. Config and codec edits follow existing patterns once the spec is admitted.

summary: The first literal Metal projection had activation first and weight second. The dense classifier fixed weight index zero, so its threshold inspected the column axis instead of the activation-row axis. Matrix roles now follow exclusive output-axis ownership and the same classifier supplies source, grid and identity.

Performance prefixes are copied from the pinned llama run context, decoded for byte validation, and never retokenized. The two build-gate arms share config, source bytes, requested roots and threshold. llama timings remain performance evidence with arithmetic and final-layer-work differences stated.

Configured paper controls returned the first hidden logit in every output channel on Metal. Dense source bakes operand roles, while the cache identity initially encoded only axes. The key now includes both roles. Same-codec reversed operands retain identical key prefixes but different role suffixes and shader reads; the repeated paper control records three distinct hidden logits within the unchanged tolerance. Retain the failed run alongside the repaired execution, rather than inferring language quality from these fixtures.

Queue::write_buffer staging was outside the proposed wgpu payload census. Configured execution now owns explicit upload buffers through synchronized completion. Literal execution records input/output/uniform/upload/readback physical rows and repeats the allocation census. Below-cap controls record zero allocation, upload, dispatch and submit counters at the actual driver sites; positive executions exercise those same counters.

Prefill and decode are execution modes; attention and feed-forward blocks run inside both. Ouro lab passes its complete uncached layer graph through Executor::prepare_with_config, including attention and feed-forward, then repeats 24 physical layers per recurrent loop with loop-boundary normalization. The dense Metal classifier is phase-agnostic: it admits product reductions by shape, storage, numeric policy and gate, not a prefill flag. Its observed paired timings cover an uncached forward/readout. Production cached decode separately uses ServingConfig and BackendRuntime, plan reuse, numeric policy and placed KV buffers through legacy named/placed planner entry points; no cached generation speedup is established by the uncached benchmark.
